name: Tragia
shared_traits: Small unisexual, petal-less flowers borne on racemes
Usually female flower(s) lower on the axis and male flowers above
look_here_first: Avoid touching the stinging plant. Photograph an intact reproductive raceme with scale, then examine leaf base, male-flower count and persistent pedicel stubs; confirm with mature capsule.

rows: Triangular-ovate serrate; truncate to cordate base
Variable; insufficient for a secure split
Short reproductive spike; inspect bracts and pedicels
Linear-lanceolate to narrowly ovate; truncate to weakly cordate

species_differences.leaf: Triangular-ovate serrate; truncate to cordate base
Variable; insufficient for a secure split
species_differences.raceme: 2–8(–10) staminate flowers; bracts 1–1.8 mm (FNA). Examine stigmatic surface and mature carpel count.
species_differences.pedicel: Persistent staminate pedicel base 0.4–1.5 mm (FNA); entirely overlaps T. ramosa, so not diagnostic alone.
species_differences.capsule: 6.5–7 mm wide (FNA); often only 1 of 3 carpels matures; capsule width overlaps T. ramosa (6–8 mm).

species_differences.leaf: Linear-lanceolate to narrowly ovate; truncate to weakly cordate

overlap_cautions: Male-flower counts and capsule sizes overlap; do not identify from one number alone.
Dark stem color is supporting evidence for T. nigricans, not proof.

FNA verifies T. brevispica staminate bracts 1–1.8 mm, persistent male pedicel bases 0.4–1.5 mm, and capsules 6.5–7 mm wide; pedicel bases and capsule widths overlap T. ramosa. Often only one capsule carpel matures, but this is not obligatory.
Do not handle stinging hairs barehanded.

FNA's strongest T. brevispica vs T. ramosa combination: often one mature carpel versus usually three; T. brevispica stigmas subpapillate to undulate and variable broad leaves, T. ramosa stigmas smooth to undulate and typically longer-than-wide narrower leaves. Stigma states overlap at undulate; fruit carpel condition is not obligatory.
lookalikes: Acalypha: pistillate bracts and divided styles rather than Tragia-style stinging racemes
Croton: stellate/scaly hairs and different inflorescence architecture
Euphorbia: cyathia instead of separate conventional unisexual flowers
Tragia urticifolia: compare persistent male pedicels and flower distribution
